rationale: Power intent is per-implementation, not protocol-level

extraction_strategy.ic_class_applicability_gate_v0_1_62: ic_class='serial_peripheral_protocol' declares LL21 not applicable; emitted as N/A stub (l_doc_taxonomy.na_stub)

low_power_modes_summary.initialization_mode: CCCR.INIT = 1; clocks running; bus output recessive.
low_power_modes_summary.power_down_sleep: Both clocks may be stopped after pending Tx + bus idle. m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA = 1.
low_power_modes_summary.bus_off: Forced shutdown after TEC = 256; CCCR.INIT set automatically; recovery requires 129 × Bus_Idle.

fields.notes: The M_CAN's power model is intentionally simple: one register-control bit (CCCR.CSR) + one pin (m_can_clkstop_req) gate the clock-stop request; the only protocol-level power feature is the clock-stop / wake-up sequence. Power-domain partitioning, retention strategy, and isolation cells are deferred to SoC + transceiver IP.

power_features.trigger_actions: When clock-stop request asserted, M_CAN completes pending transmissions, waits for bus idle, sets CCCR.INIT = 1 internally, then asserts m_can_clkstop_ack + CCCR.CSA = 1.
power_features.abort_path: If bus is heavily disturbed and idle never reached, CCCR.INIT remains 0; software polls PSR.ACT and may write CCCR.INIT = 1 explicitly.
wake_up_procedure: 1. External clock controller restarts m_can_hclk + m_can_cclk.
2. CPU deasserts m_can_clkstop_req or clears CCCR.CSR.
5. BSP waits for 11 consecutive recessive bits.

dual_clock_domain_concept.m_can_hclk: Host clock domain — Tx Handler / Rx Handler / Generic Slave / Generic Master / RAM Watchdog. May be FM-PLL spread spectrum.
dual_clock_domain_concept.m_can_cclk: CAN clock domain — CAN Core / BSP / BTL. Must be high-precision.
dual_clock_domain_concept.frequency_constraint: m_can_hclk frequency ≥ m_can_cclk frequency (spread-spectrum modulation depth must also be considered).
dual_clock_domain_concept.sync_block: Synchronizes signals + reset across the two domains.

fields.interrupt_during_power_down: The two CPU interrupt lines reflect IR + IE + ILS + ILE state. During clock-stop, no new IR flags are set; existing latched flags remain visible until host clears them.
